item.title: Multifidelity Data Fusion for Hypersonic Heating: Experiments Meet AI
item.description: Duan and colleagues introduce an augmented data fusion framework aimed at predicting aerodynamic heating on hypersonic vehicles. This framework…
item.content:encoded:
Type: 🤖 ML/Heating Prediction | Relevance: 88/100

Duan and colleagues introduce an augmented data fusion framework aimed at predicting aerodynamic heating on hypersonic vehicles. This framework combines data enhancement strategies with a multifidelity U-NET (MF-UNet) architecture. The approach addresses the challenges of sparse experimental data and the inherent trade-offs in accuracy and resolution associated with traditional CFD and wind-tunnel measurements. The MF-UNet is developed to optimize multifidelity mapping for high-precision heat-flux reconstruction, while systematic data augmentation expands limited experimental datasets to improve extrapolation capabilities.

The methodology was validated on a hypersonic double-ellipsoid configuration. It successfully integrated three sparse experimental datasets to generate complete surface heating profiles. The framework demonstrated significant improvements over baseline CFD solutions, achieving a surface-averaged normalized root-mean-square error below 3% when compared with experimental measurements. The approach enables full-surface extrapolation, even with limited experimental inputs.

This work provides a practical solution for aerodynamic heating analysis by effectively integrating multifidelity data, particularly sparse experimental measurements, with a deep learning model. The ability to generate complete heating profiles and extrapolate to new conditions from limited experimental data is valuable for design cycles where experimental campaigns are costly and time-consuming.

item.title: Simplifying High-Enthalpy Nitrogen Flow: VVT vs. VTm for Aerodynamic Heating
item.description: This paper investigates the impact of vibration–vibration–translation (VVT) reactions in state-to-state (StS) simulations of high-enthalpy nitrogen…
item.content:encoded:
Type: 💻 Numerical/CFD | Relevance: 75/100

This paper investigates the impact of vibration–vibration–translation (VVT) reactions in state-to-state (StS) simulations of high-enthalpy nitrogen flow over a sphere. The primary objective is to reduce the significant computational cost associated with detailed StS simulations by evaluating two simplification methods: multiquantum restrictions and simplifying VVT transitions to vibration–translation (VTm) transitions. This work extends a previous study, systematically analyzing how these transition models affect flowfield characteristics and, crucially, heat flux distributions.

The numerical results demonstrate that both the full StS VVT model and the simplified VTm model predict nearly identical shock standoff distances and stagnation-point heat fluxes. These predictions align well with available experimental data. When comparing VVT and VTm transitions, the study finds minimal differences in the predictions of translational temperature, vibrational temperature, and nitrogen mass fraction. Near the wall, both models yield almost identical state populations, which exhibit gradually pronounced non-Boltzmann distributions.

The key finding is that VVT transitions can be effectively reduced to VTm transitions without compromising essential accuracy for predicting aerodynamic heating in this high-enthalpy nitrogen flow scenario. This outcome is valuable for the aerothermodynamics community, as it offers a practical approach to decrease the computational burden of detailed state-to-state simulations, making them more feasible for multidimensional applications while maintaining accuracy in critical heating predictions.

This paper review was generated by Gemini 2.5 Flash and curated by AeroSentinel v2.5.0.

Reference

  1. Xiaoyong Wang, Qiming Zhang, Ming Che et al., “Effects of vibration–vibration–translation reactions in vibrational state-specific modeling of high-enthalpy nitrogen flow over a sphere,” Physics of Fluids, 2026-03-01. Link
